newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat eases on Chicago, USDA report.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat eases on Chicago, USDA report.

text.p: Australian wheat futures fell moderately on Tuesday in line with Chicago's overnight fall and on lessened supply fears after the latest USDA figures.
January 1998 was the only contract to trade, selling five lots at A$185.00 a tonne, down A$3.50 on the trade.

Settlement prices mostly came back by 50 cents to A$2.50, apart from a A$21.50 fall by the erratic September 1998 contract. The exceptions were the two nearest-term contracts, which both rose by A$2.50 a tonne to recoup Monday's losses.
Kerrin Gleeson of Elders Risk Management said the SFE market eased following Chicago, the fall of rain in Europe and lower demand in the U.S. as shown in the USDA report.
Easing demand was not pressuring tight stocks, as had been feared before the latest USDA report, she said.
